hints.title: Product Growth Bound
hints.text: Subarray products outpace least common multiples rapidly unless restricted to small ranges.

hints.title: Subarray Traversal
hints.text: Iterate all subarray start indices and extend ending indices while updating running product, greatest common divisor, and least common multiple.

hints.title: Equivalence Test
hints.text: Verify prod(arr) == lcm(arr) * gcd(arr) at each extension and track maximum contiguous length.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def maxLength(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        max_len = 0
        for i in range(n):
            prod = 1
            curr_gcd = 0
            curr_lcm = 1
            for j in range(i, n):
                val = nums[j]
                prod *= val
                curr_gcd = math.gcd(curr_gcd, val) if curr_gcd else val
                curr_lcm = (curr_lcm * val) // math.gcd(curr_lcm, val)
                if prod == curr_gcd * curr_lcm:
                    max_len = max(max_len, j - i + 1)
        return max_len
```

complexity.notes: Double loop scanning all subarrays with logarithmic greatest common divisor and least common multiple updates.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing greatest common divisor and least common multiple from scratch yields cubic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) auxiliary memory maintains running math variables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Incrementally updates product, greatest common divisor, and least common multiple in nested loop.
